blocks: Title: Black & Grey Realism Tattoo Manchester | Vladimir Vishar
Meta description: Black and grey realism tattoos in Manchester & Salford. Dramatic contrast, smooth shading, photorealistic detail by Vladimir Vishar. Hourly rate £140.
Black & Grey Realism Tattoo Manchester | Vladimir Vishar
Skip to main content
Home / Black and Grey Realism Manchester
Timeless monochrome realism — dramatic contrast, smooth shading, and photorealistic detail.
Manchester & Salford · £140/hr · Currently booking September – October 2026
Enquiry via No Regrets Manchester. The team will arrange an in-person or video consultation with me before any tattoo session is booked.
The Art of Monochrome

Black and grey realism transforms diluted black ink into a full tonal spectrum — from the softest whisper of grey to the deepest shadow. The result is tattoo work that looks like a high-contrast black-and-white photograph rendered directly on skin.

This style excels with subjects that thrive on dramatic lighting : portraits, religious iconography, mythology, wildlife, dark realism and horror-inspired pieces, and architectural scenes. Every piece I create is custom-designed to follow the natural contours of your body, using light and shadow to create depth that feels genuinely three-dimensional.
From pure white skin tones through soft mid-greys to deep black — the complete greyscale spectrum in every piece.
Bold shadows and sharp highlights that create cinematic depth — the hallmark of strong black and grey work.
Black and grey tattoos soften naturally over time, developing a smoky quality that many find even more appealing than fresh.
Black & Grey Portfolio
Selected works in monochrome realism
View full portfolio →
From concept to completed piece
Share your idea — subject, references, placement, size. I'll give you an honest assessment, time estimate, and a clear plan.
Every design is created specifically for your body — anatomy, muscle flow, how it looks from different angles. You'll see the design on session day.
Sessions run up to 7 hours. Black and grey realism builds up gradually — structure first, then depth, shadow, and smooth transitions.
Proper healing preserves contrast and detail. Full aftercare guide provided.
Other specialities
Vivid photorealistic colour — portraits, wildlife, florals.
Transforming old ink into something you'll be proud of.
How long does a black and grey realism tattoo take?

Black and grey realism is usually slightly faster than colour realism, but it still needs careful structure, contrast, smooth shading, and detail. As a rough guide: forearm or smaller areas usually take 1–2 full-day sessions; shoulder or upper arm usually takes 2–3 full-day sessions; and a full arm sleeve usually takes 6–8+ sessions. Larger areas are estimated after reviewing your idea, placement, size, skin, and references.
Does black and grey realism age better than colour?
Black and grey tattoos age gracefully. The tones soften naturally, often developing a smoky quality that many find appealing. With proper aftercare and SPF, they hold detail and contrast for decades.
What subjects work best in black and grey?

Portraits, religious and mythological scenes, wildlife, skulls, clocks, roses, dark realism and horror-inspired pieces, and architectural elements all work exceptionally well. Any subject with strong contrast and tonal range is ideal for this style.
Can you add colour accents to a black and grey tattoo?
Yes. Selective colour — coloured eyes, a red rose, a blue sky — creates a striking focal point within monochrome work. We'll discuss the best approach in your consultation.
How much does a black and grey realism tattoo cost?

My hourly rate is £140. I give an estimate after reviewing your idea, placement, size, skin, and references. Smaller 3–4 hour projects may be possible if the idea fits, but most medium and large black and grey realism work is planned as full-day sessions.
What references should I send for a black and grey realism tattoo?

Send your idea, placement, approximate size, photos of the area if useful, subject photos, mood/style references, and examples of contrast or lighting you like. I build the design around body flow, scale, readability, skin, and placement limits. I do not use templates or repeat designs.
Difference between black and grey realism and blackwork?

Black and grey realism uses diluted ink to create a full tonal range mimicking photography. Blackwork uses solid black for bold graphic designs and patterns. Fundamentally different techniques and aesthetics.
Let's build your piece.
Currently booking September – October 2026

Send me your idea and references. I'll reply with an honest assessment, time estimate, and clear next steps. After your concept has been reviewed and you decide to book, No Regrets Studios requires a non-refundable chair rental fee to secure the appointment. This comes off the overall tattoo cost.
No Regrets Studios, Manchester / Salford
